coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Only duty is MISSA Social Security/Health Fund employer contributions (secondary guide: quarterly returns due within 10 days of quarter end, monthly wage reports by the 15th). Nothing new beyond K07.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No search spent; budget used on regulator-first breadth. No scrap licensing regime surfaced incidentally.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No search spent; nothing surfaced incidentally.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Only touched via the Banking Act 2017 DNFBP definition (dealers in precious metals and stones). No licence register or reporting form found. See candidate on DNFBP AML.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No search spent. Only vehicle registration history surfaced (Police Dept data 2004-2008); no dismantler regime found.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Atoll microstate with negligible commercial livestock trade; no evidence of a regulated livestock market. Not searched.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No search spent; nothing surfaced.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No beekeeping sector expected on coral atolls. Not searched.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: No search spent; nothing surfaced.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No search spent. Water is rainwater and desalination, mostly utility-run (MWSC), so low likelihood.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Majuro Atoll Waste Company is a state-owned monopoly collector. Solid Waste Regulations 1989 and Environmental Protection Act 1984 are still the framework; no new 2024-2025 used-oil or battery rule found. Used lead-acid battery buy-back is a SPREP/EU donor programme. Nothing viable.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No search spent; nothing surfaced.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No search spent; nothing surfaced.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: No search spent; nothing surfaced.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Only seafarer recruitment and placement services under the RMI Maritime Administrator Marine Notice 7-045-1 (June 2024, MLC 2006 amendments). The duty falls on shipowners and operators, and the agencies are mostly foreign. Mapped to K03/K05, which were rejected. No local labour-contractor licensing regime found.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No search spent; nothing surfaced.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Non-Profit Entities Act 2020 (in force 14 May 2021; amended 2021) replaced the Non-Profit Corporation Act. A commercial guide says an annual report is filed with the Registrar of Corporations (window opens 1 Jan). Churches have no registration requirement (2015 US report, dated). Weak candidate logged; no halal or kosher supervision.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Domestic Watercraft Act 1992 (47 MIRC Ch.9): registration and licensing of domestic vessels under the Minister of Transportation and Communications and the Maritime Administrator. MISCO runs outer-island shipping and may hire smaller vessels. A public vessel register from MTC (2015 data) exists. No current taxi or bus licence rules found; the Majuro taxi trade is informal. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Local government business licences are capped by the Local Government Tax and Fees Act (4 MIRC Ch.2) to reasonable registration fees. No market-trader or street-vendor regime or e-filing found. Money remitters fall under the Banking Commission (see DNFBP candidate).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: No childcare or nursery licensing regime found for RMI. Private (non-public) schools need annual accreditation or charter under the Education Act 1991 s.336 (only an education-profiles.org summary plus a commercial guide). No tattoo, driving-school or hunting regime found. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: The market is concentrated. State-owned MEC imports and distributes diesel, LPG and lubricants (and is moving into gasoline), with an import-duty exemption under the 2008 MEC Exemption Act. Mobil used to supply gasoline. No private fuel-licensing or price-regulator regime found. Nothing for a small-business tool.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: The only commodity is copra via Tobolar. Nothing new beyond K06.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: No search spent. No co-operative or credit-union regulator surfaced.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Only one private clinic and one private optometry practice in Majuro (HRSA 2022). The Health Fund is run by the Ministry of Health and funded via MISSA. The off-island medical referral programme has been suspended at times over unpaid bills. Buyer group is too small and the payer is the state. Nothing viable.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: No pharmacy act or pharmacist-licensing law found. The Narcotic Drugs (Prohibition and Control) Act 1987 makes the Government the sole importer and distributor of narcotics. Nothing viable.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No local manpower-agency regime found. Only the seafarer recruitment and placement angle (see 15).

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: No search spent; nothing surfaced.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Banking (Amendment) Act 2017 defines DNFBPs (casinos, real estate agents, precious metals and stones dealers, lawyers, accountants, trust and company service providers). The Banking Commission is AML supervisor and FIU. Reporting forms, thresholds and registration for DNFBPs were not found. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: The Marshall Islands Visitors Authority Act 1997 defines 'tourist facility'. No guest-register or tourism-levy rule found. Few small lodgings.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Marine Resources Act 1997 and Fisheries Regulations 1998 license types: fishing vessel, live fish capture, fish export facility, aquaculture, plus export certification. Fisheries agent port-entry is already covered (K02, rejected on the MIMRA Web App). Local reef and aquarium export licensees are very few. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 31. Gross revenue tax and wage-tax filers (Income Tax Act as amended: P.L. 2022-44 monthly GRT, Bill 103 P.L. 2026-68)
coverage.found: The 2022 amendment changed GRT from quarterly to monthly, with s.110A letting compliant firms apply for quarterly filing. Bill 103 (March 2026) revises wage tax (sources conflict on the details). The IMF's 2025 technical-assistance report proposes a VAT, with no enactment found. All already known (K01, K04).

coverage.category: 32. Foreign Investment Business Licence holders (non-citizen-owned businesses)
coverage.found: FIBL Act and Regulations (2000, amended 19 Dec 2019, plus 2019 amendment Act). Licence holders must notify the Registrar of register changes within 30 days and must show a valid FIBL to local councils. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 33. Alcohol and tobacco import licensees
coverage.found: Import Duties Act 1989 Part II (2004 amendment) requires Secretary of Finance licences for alcohol and tobacco importers, deliberately limited in number. The Alcoholic Beverage Control Act 21 MIRC Ch.1 covers retail licences, but the text and fees were not seen. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 34. Domestic watercraft owners and inter-island boat operators
coverage.found: See 18. The Domestic Watercraft Act 1992 covers registration, inspection and seafarer ID. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 35. Non-profit entities (Non-Profit Entities Act 2020)
coverage.found: See 17.

coverage.category: 36. Importers declaring under ASYCUDAWorld customs system (live 2024)
coverage.found: The Customs Division moved to ASYCUDAWorld (UNCTAD, EU IMPACT project). Importers and brokers must use this state portal. No customs-broker licensing regime found. Weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 37. Private schools and early childhood centres (Education Act 1991 accreditation)
coverage.found: See 20. Candidate logged as weak.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Scrap Metal Dealer Inspection Act 2009 (P.L. 2009-14, 8 MIRC Ch. 8) exists: dealers must keep a record of every purchase/sale transaction, and records must be presented to a law-enforcement officer designated by the Minister of Justice before any export. No dealer registration or periodic filing found (no registration section in the contents). Scrap is exported in volume (about 1,100 t over 2014-16). PacLII text blocked (403), so record fields and penalties are unverified. Source: https://paclii.org/mh/legis/consol_act/smdia2009272 (search snippet).

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Marshall Islands pawnbroker or second-hand dealer statute or licence found. No national business-names or sole-trader register (secondary source, infoproff). Nothing new beyond general business licensing.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler, abandoned-vehicle or end-of-life vehicle regime found. Only vehicle registration (Police Dept) and Majuro Solid Waste Management Plan 2019-2028 / Solid Waste Regulation 1989 (EPA) surfaced as possible hooks. Unverified whether either covers derelict vehicles.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Only the Export Meat Inspection Act (8 MIRC Ch. 2), which covers export meat and carries a business registration provision. It is irrelevant to the domestic market, which is mostly imported meat under the Plant and Animal Quarantine Regulations. No domestic slaughterhouse or butcher licensing found.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Only the quarantine side surfaced: the Quarantine Division of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Commerce handles animal import permits (dog/cat Animal Permit Application) under the Plant and Animal Quarantine Regulations (8 MIRC Ch. 3). No veterinary practice or veterinary-medicine seller regime found. No resident private vet found in the searches.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No well-drilling permit or groundwater abstraction regime found. Majuro's Dalap-Uliga-Darrit area depends on airstrip rainwater catchment; the freshwater lens is shallow (boreholes 5-10 m). Utility-run (MWSC). Nothing for private operators.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Marshall Islands boiler, pressure-vessel or elevator inspection law found in two searches (results were US states). The National Building Code Act 2025 (P.L. 36-2025) covers 'certain equipment' and creates a Building Inspector, which could pull in lifts, but scope is unverified. Few buildings with lifts exist in the country.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nothing found on small-system drinking-water regulation or private operators. The water context is rainwater catchment and the utility MWSC. Not pursued further.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: RMI EPA Pesticides and POPs Regulations 2004, made under the National Environmental Protection Act 1984 (ss. 21, 63). Part III certifies private and commercial applicators, Part IV requires a permit to deal in restricted-use pesticides, Part V requires record-keeping by commercial applicators and licensed dealers, Part VI covers notice of intent to import and inspection. Full text and fees were not retrievable (403/503). Buyer count looks tiny (a handful of dealers, few commercial applicators).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No cemetery or funeral licensing found. Burial is customary, on family or landowner (alap) land, with no payment. Ebeye cemeteries are full (2010 report). No regulated business class to sell to.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Cooperative associations are in 18 MIRC Ch. 1 (Title 18 Cooperatives and Non-Profit Corporations); the registrar and any annual filing were not seen (contents only). No credit-union regulator or credit-union sector found. Microfinance goes through BOMI and the Marshall Islands Development Bank with Taiwan ICDF funding. Tiny, non-viable as a software market.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: New National Building Code Act 2025 (P.L. 36-2025, Bill 39, 46th Nitijela) sets minimum standards for design, construction, materials, occupancy, location and maintenance, with a Building Inspector, other inspectors and a Building Committee. RMI code is based on the 2018 IBC (adopted 2019). A World Bank-financed tender (RMI Urban Resilience Project, deadline 14 Aug 2026) is for technical assistance to implement the code at the Ministry of Public Works and Infrastructure building safety division. No contractor licensing or registration regime confirmed. Full Act text blocked (403), so permit, contractor and commencement provisions are unverified. Quarry and mining: nothing found.

decisions.reason: Same buyers and same duty as K01 (RMI gross revenue tax filing); monthly cadence is only detail.
Same employers and same MISSA quarterly return duty as K07.
Same employers and same Bill 103 wage-tax change as K04.
New buyer and duty: foreign-owned small firms with FIBL renewals and 30-day change notices.
New duty: alcohol and tobacco licensees, small firms with licence compliance; verifiers can judge market size.
New buyer: domestic boat owners with registration and inspection duty, unlike K03's RMI-flag ship tooling. Related to K03.
New buyer: non-profits and community bodies with annual registry filings; the duty still needs checking.
Small professional offices and dealers carry AML/CFT duties; the buyer group is new.
Different buyer and duty from K02: local fishing and export licence holders, not port-entry agents. Related to K02.
Buyers are global shipowners and manning agencies for RMI-flag ships, the same market and duty as K03/K05.
New buyer and duty: small importers and brokers making customs declarations.
New buyer: small non-public schools and preschools with a recurring annual accreditation duty.
New buyer and duty: small shops and vendors holding local council licences.
No mandatory recurring duty to an authority was found, and the buy-back is donor-run, so it fails the candidate definition.
Duty falls on small builders and owners under the new code; the ministry as buyer is a verifier question.
Dealers have a real record-keeping and pre-export inspection duty; the buyer count is small but new.
New buyer and duty: pesticide dealers and applicators with permit and record-keeping duties.
New buyer: cooperatives; the annual duty is unconfirmed, so verifiers should check it.
